title: Cookwala Mission
description: The shared, signed, living document of the Cookwala Protocol (docs/PROTOCOL.md): intent, mandate, context facets, credentials, routing, requirements with criticality, fallbacks (PACE), decision rights, escalation, contributions with commitment lifecycle, the bound plan, execution, outcome and a hash-chained ledger. Decision governance is described in docs/DECISIONS.md.

holder.description: DID of the party that owns the Mission (usually the robot acting for the household); only the holder accepts contributions and closes the Mission.

owner.description: DID of the human/organization the holder acts for.

parent.description: Parent Mission (e.g. a relief program Mission).

commandersIntent.description: What matters most if the plan breaks (e.g. 'a safe, warm halal dinner for 5 by 19:30; cost matters more than variety').

priorities.description: Order after the fixed safety prefix; the first three are always first.

advice.description: Structured request when the intent maps to a reasoner intent.

mandate.description: What the holder may do and decide.

mayAddParties.description: Providers/people the holder may bring into the flow.

authority.description: Whose instructions win (higher level wins within scope).

groups.description: Provider groups that share capabilities (consortia, ensembles, partner networks).

mode.description: Each member answers independently, the group returns one agreed answer, or a leader answers and others review.

readiness.description: Definition of ready: execution may start only when every listed requirement is satisfied (or resolved by an allowed fallback) and the safety kernel passes.

budgets.description: Guardrails for cost, time, energy, retries, hops, data disclosure, human attention. Tracked live from contributions, meters and execution; thresholds trigger actions automatically.

meters.description: Accruals against budgets (each also recorded in the ledger).

roles.description: Who plays which role in this Mission (see docs/DECISIONS.md).

degradations.description: What is not working fully right now (robot, environment, devices, connectivity). Declared by the holder or observed by monitors.

adaptations.description: How the plan is adjusted to the degradations, by whom, with which accepted deviations from the normal dish.

eventLog.description: Where the authoritative event log lives and which head this projection was derived from.

ProviderSlot.description: A role in the flow with ordered candidates (primary → alternates), what each may see and do.

role.description: e.g. planner, grocer, delivery, monitor, arbiter:substitution, nutrition, orchestrator.

view.description: Facet types disclosed to this role.

hedge.description: Ask alternates in parallel when latency matters; first valid answer wins.

capabilities.description: Capability tags this role covers, e.g. estimate:robot_energy, estimate:duration, assess:criticality. Several roles/providers may share a tag; their outputs become competing assessments.

Criticality.description: critical: must be met exactly, never traded, failure blocks the Mission (allergen-free, halal, CCPs, child safety). required: must be met, but approved alternatives (plan B/C) are allowed. preferred: degrade gracefully; record the loss. optional: drop silently if unavailable; log only.

what.description: e.g. ingredient:eggs, dietary:halal, allergen_free:peanuts, serve_by:19:30, budget<=40USD, dish_identity, delivery:groceries, device:oven.

source.description: Who set it: owner, recipe identity, policy pack, clinician, mode.

decidedBy.description: Decision class governing changes to it (see decisionRights).

Pace.description: Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency (military PACE planning): ordered plan A/B/C/D for one requirement, step or the whole Mission.

action.description: e.g. substitute:cw.ing.turmeric, provider:did:web:grocer-b, method:pressure_cook, dish:w-ma-012, order:ready_meal, drop, delay:PT30M, ask:owner.

trigger.description: When to switch: timeout, unavailable, failed_check, budget_exceeded, quality_below.

needsApproval.description: Decision class or actor that must approve before switching.

DecisionRight.description: Who may decide what. Evaluated top-down; the first matching rule applies. Safety-class decisions can never be granted solely to a remote provider.

limits.description: Thresholds under which the decider may act alone, e.g. {"extraCost": {"amount": 3, "currency": "USD"}, "quality": "minor", "delay": "PT15M"}.

beyondLimits.description: Decision class/actor to escalate to when limits are exceeded.

to.description: holder | arbiter:<class> | orchestrator | household:<person/role> | maker_support | service_provider | emergency_services.

Contribution.description: What a provider adds. Lifecycle: offered → accepted/rejected (by holder) → committed (binding, with SLA) → in_progress → fulfilled | partially_fulfilled | failed | withdrawn | superseded | compensated.

compensation.description: Action that undoes/offsets this contribution if the Mission changes (cancel order, release slot, refund) — saga pattern.

needs.description: Missing facets/permissions that would let it succeed.

Closure.description: How the Mission ends: every committed contribution is fulfilled, failed-and-compensated or released; the holder signs the final receipt; settlements are recorded.

anchoredAt.description: Transparency log / blockchain anchoring reference, if any.

calibration.description: Predicted vs actual per assessment; updates provider calibration and reputation.

LedgerEntry.description: Append-only, hash-chained, signed. Modeled on EPCIS event dimensions (what, when, where, why, who). Deprecated in favour of MissionEvent (same fields plus hash); kept for 0.1 documents.

prev.description: Hash of the previous entry ('genesis' for seq 0).

scope.description: Whole mission, a requirement, a step, a provider role or a provider (e.g. 'mission', 'role:grocer', 'step:n7').

unit.description: Currency code, ISO 8601 duration ('time'), kWh, MJ, L, pct, count, minutes.

limit.description: Hard limit (number, Money or Duration/DateTime for time).

at.description: Fraction of limit (0.8 = 80%) or of forecast overrun.

on.description: Trigger on spent-so-far or on estimate-at-completion.

to.description: Who is notified/asked (decision class, role or person).

controller.description: Who tracks and enforces it: holder (default), orchestrator (delegated), or budget_controller provider. The holder's kernel enforces hard limits regardless.

committed.description: Committed but not yet spent (e.g. accepted orders).

forecastAtCompletion.description: Estimate at completion (spent + committed + remaining plan).

carryOver.description: Unspent amount returns to a parent budget (meal plan, week).

affects.description: Ops, sensors or cues affected (cw.op.cut, cw.sense.translucent...).

by.description: Who proposed/provides it: holder, planner, arbiter, maker extension, another robot, smart-home device, human, teleoperation service.

actions.description: e.g. 'turn on hood light (Matter On/Off)', 'use probe cw.sense.core_temp instead of vision cue', 'arm-1 camera streams view of pan', 'coarse chop 20 mm instead of 10 mm'.

deviation.description: How the result will differ from the normal dish.

identityPreserved.description: Must be true unless a change_dish decision approved otherwise.

sensory.description: e.g. 'onions less browned', 'coarser texture', 'slightly overcooked eggs (firm yolks)'.

safety.description: Why safety is unchanged or stricter (never looser).

Assessment.description: An opinion, estimate or judgment by a provider (or the robot) on a topic. Multiple providers may assess the same topic; they may agree, refine or disagree.

topic.description: e.g. estimate.robot_energy_pct, estimate.robot_energy_wh, estimate.duration, estimate.cost, estimate.appliance_energy_kwh, assess.safety, assess.criticality, assess.feasibility, assess.doneness, assess.spoilage.

subject.description: What it is about: mission, recipe, plan, task, item.

inputsHash.description: Hash of the inputs/view it saw, so disagreements caused by different inputs are visible.

calibration.description: Provider's historical accuracy on this topic (claimed; verified by the reconciler from closure data).

reconciler.description: holder (default), a chosen agent/orchestrator DID, a quorum, or a household human.

safetyBias.description: For safety/feasibility topics take the cautious quantile (e.g. energy need at p90).

conflictThreshold.description: Relative spread above which assessments count as conflicting (e.g. 0.25).

evidenceOrder.description: Precedence when evidence quality differs, e.g. [measurement, historical_stats, physics_model, vendor_spec, llm_judgment].

rounds.description: Requests for more evidence/rebuttals (e.g. robot measured battery; provider re-estimated).

decisionValue.description: The value used for decisions after safety bias.

consequences.description: Decision/plan-change ids triggered (charge first, handoff midway, notify owner...).

MissionEvent.description: One entry of the Mission event log. The log is the source of truth; the Mission document is a projection derived by replaying it (tools/mission_reducer.py). One sequencer per Mission (normally the holder's hub) assigns seq and prev, so the chain never forks; other parties submit proposals and receive the sequenced event back.

payload.description: Type-specific body. Personal content may be replaced by a Disclosure digest.

payloadDigest.description: Hash-only mode: the payload is stored off-log in erasable storage and only its hash is kept here.

hash.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of this event without hash and signature.

proposedBy.description: When the actor is not the sequencer: the actor's signature over the proposal.

Checkpoint.description: A signed statement of the log head, counter-signed by witnesses (another party in the Mission or an external transparency service, e.g. IETF SCITT). A sequencer that rewrites history after a witnessed checkpoint is detectable.
